minor-latin;mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-latin'>UCA 26B-4-213</span></i></a><span
class=normaltextrun><i><span style='font-size:11.0pt;font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif;
mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-fareast-font-family:"Times New Roman";
mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-latin'> currently
prohibits a recommending medical provider from recommending medical cannabis to
a patient through a virtual visit with certain exceptions. Recommendations are
permitted through a virtual visit if the patient (1) is on hospice or has a
terminal illness; (2) is a resident of an assisted living facility or nursing
care facility; (3) has previously received a medical cannabis recommendation
from the recommending medical provider through a face-to-face visit; or (4) is
a current patient of the recommending medical provider and has met with the
recommending medical provider face-to-face previously. The Working Group will
consider the virtual visit recommendation policy.<o:p></o:p></span></i></span></p>

mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold"'>Out-of-state Marijuana Entity
Advertising<o:p></o:p></span></b></p>

<p class=MsoListParagraphCxSpMiddle><i>Utah statute places various parameters
on how, what, and to whom state licensed medical cannabis entities are permitted
to advertise. Concerns have been raised that out-of-state marijuana entities
are currently placing advertisements in Utah for products that would be
otherwise illegal within the state of Utah. The Working Group will consider
these concerns and policy proposals to address these concerns.<o:p></o:p></i></p>

– 2:15PM<o:p></o:p></span></b></p>

<p class=AgendaItemExplanationText>The committee will hear a report on security
systems at community water systems, including information regarding security
incidents, emergency response plans, and any recommendations to improve
security at community water systems, per H.B. 19, Drinking Water Utilities
Amendments, 2026 General Session.</p>

<p class=AgendaItemExplanationText>The committee will hear a report from the
Utah Broadband Center on the statewide digital connectivity plan per Utah Code
Section 72-19-203.</p>

<p class=AgendaItemExplanationText>The committee will hear a report from the

<p class=AgendaItemExplanationText>The committee will hear a report from the
Utah Energy Council on the council’s activities per Utah Code Section 79-6-1103,
including an update on designated electrical energy development zones and an
update on the Intermountain Power Agency’s Request for Proposals (RFP) process
regarding the potential sale, transfer, or other disposition of the
Intermountain Power Plant coal units.</p>

<p class=MsoListParagraph style='margin-bottom:0in;line-height:normal;
tab-stops:226.5pt'><i><span style='font-family:"Franklin Gothic Book",sans-serif;
mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>Under </span></i><a
href="https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title63G/Chapter3/63G-3-S301.html?v=C63G-3-S301_2026050620260506"><i><span
style='font-family:"Franklin Gothic Book",sans-serif;mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";
mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>Utah Code Annotated § 63G-3-301</span></i></a><i><span
style='font-family:"Franklin Gothic Book",sans-serif;mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";
mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>, rulemaking entities are required to prepare a
fiscal impact statement for rules detailing the rule’s anticipated cost or
savings to the state budget, local governments, small businesses, and other
persons. Rulemaking agencies are required to notify the Legislature before
making a rule effective if the rule’s anticipated cost is greater than $1
million, and agencies are generally prohibited from enacting rules with an
anticipated cost greater than $2 million. The committee will conduct a review
of a recent rule proposal by the Department of Transportation (UDOT) to amend Utah
Administrative Code R909-19 in light of the fiscal impact requirements, and
consider whether statutory changes are necessary to ensure rulemaking
procedures align with legislative intent.<o:p></o:p></span></i></p>

<p class=MsoListParagraph style='margin-bottom:0in;line-height:normal;

mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>Under Utah
Administrative Code R313-25, the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) is
required to maintain current performance assessment standards for depleted
uranium disposal that reflect ongoing guidance and rulemaking from the Nuclear
Regulatory Commission (NRC). The committee will receive presentations from
industry participants and DEQ officials covering implementation of these rule
provisions and how they interact with recent rule proposals made by the NRC.<o:p></o:p></span></i></p>

<p class=MsoListParagraph style='margin-bottom:0in;line-height:normal;

mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>During the
2025 General Session, the Legislature enacted </span></i><a

style='font-family:"Franklin Gothic Book",sans-serif;mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";
mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>S.B. 330, "Cosmetology Modifications"</span></i></a><i><span
style='font-family:"Franklin Gothic Book",sans-serif;mso-bidi-font-family:"Segoe UI Semibold";
mso-bidi-font-weight:bold'>, which restructures and modifies several provisions
for licensing standards for the Cosmetology and Associated Professions
Licensing Act (“Act”). On October 1<sup>st</sup>, the Division of Professional
Licensing (DOPL) published a proposal to repeal and readopt Utah Administrative
Code R156-11a, the associated administrative rule for the Act, with changes to
reflect statutory modifications made by the Legislature. The committee will
receive presentations from industry participants and DOPL staff covering the
proposed changes and review them to determine whether the changes comply with
